answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, and memory_73 looks like strong support (31% paid conversion lift, 18% revenue lift). But that record is exactly where the inherited summary is thinnest in the direction that matters: a 12-week observation window with an unchanged support model cannot tell us whether discount-acquired, price-sensitive accounts retain, expand, or generate qualified revenue past the promo period. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching a price attack is also the move most likely to reset our price anchor permanently and pull in exactly the churn-prone cohort the competitor is targeting. So memory_73 is my first verification pull \, I want the original record to see whether retention/quality were measured at all or simply not observed.

My current intent is simplify_onboarding. It is the only direction supported by two independent inherited records (memory_31 on signup-field reduction driving durable SMB activation lift, memory_86 on shortened onboarding improving completion and time-to-value), and it targets both of the actually-observed regressions this quarter: activation down 6% and onboarding completion down 4%. Those declines are internal and within our control, whereas the competitor's pricing is not. Improving activation also raises the value we deliver before any pricing conversation, which is the more defensible response to a price attack than a counter-discount. memory_91 (activation messaging) is adjacent and plausible, but it addresses only the activation symptom, while onboarding simplification plausibly moves both.

Second verification pull is memory_86, because it is the record I am about to act on and I should not lean hardest on the memory I have checked least. I want to know the segment it was run in (self-serve only?), the effect size, whether the lift was durable or a novelty bump, and whether "completion rate" improved by genuinely reducing friction or by removing steps that were doing qualification work \, if we stripped fields that filtered out low-intent accounts, we would be buying completion metrics with worse downstream lead quality, the same class of error I am worried about with promotional_pricing.

Caveats I am carrying rather than resolving: all six memories are consolidated summaries whose sources I have not read, and none of them are timestamped against the current competitive environment \, memory_31 is 64 days old and conditions have shifted. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout, with activation and downstream qualified-revenue quality as tracked outcomes, not just completion rate. If memory_86's source shows the lift came from removing qualification signal, I will fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91) instead. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is likely correct but does not address the SMB segment under attack this week.
